focus: A16 release cadence, pinning and what "perfect" can promise: npm dist-tags and publish times for opencode-ai, @opencode/cli, @opencode/plugin and @opencode-ai/plugin; v2 stability/beta statements; minimum supported versions, pinning strategy, runtime detection, support window and honest limits

label: The latest-1 dist-tag is NOT a v1 maintenance signal and falsifies the iteration premise: opencode-ai latest-1 resolves to 1.1.4, an early-1.x line, while opencode-ai latest resolves to 1.19.3. v1 maintenance must be read from opencode-ai@latest and @opencode-ai/plugin@latest, both 1.19.3 published 2026-10-16T12:32Z, the same day as the newest v2 publish; the v1 line is actively maintained.

Release-cadence table: v1 1.18.x shipped 36 versions 2026-07-14 to 2026-10-06 (84 days, ~0.43/day); v1 1.19.x shipped 4 versions 2026-10-11 to 2026-10-16 (5 days, ~0.80/day); v2 2.0.x shipped 33 versions 2026-09-11 to 2026-10-16 (35 days, ~0.94/day). Total 1.x versions 458; total 2.x versions 33, all inside the single minor 2.0.x. v2 ships at more than double the v1 1.18 cadence and has never left 2.0.

v1 and v2 live in different npm scopes: v1 is opencode-ai plus @opencode-ai/plugin (latest 1.19.3); v2 is @opencode/cli plus @opencode/plugin (latest 2.0.32). The repo pins only @opencode-ai/plugin 1.18.34 in .opencode/package.json and .skilled/package.json, and neither @opencode/cli nor @opencode/plugin appears anywhere in the repo, so a v2-only install gets no v2 type surface at all and no rename can fix it because the v2 package has a different name.

The 1.18.34 pin predates the v2-aware v1 line: 1.18.34 published 2026-09-30, then 1.18.35 on 2026-10-06 and 1.19.0 on 2026-10-11, so the pin is one patch behind the end of its own minor and three releases behind the targeted 1.19.x line. Every v1-side plugin-contract measurement taken against 1.18.34 in iterations 1-3 describes a host that is not the target host and is valid only as a lower bound.

v2 publishes no stability, beta or semver guarantee and v1 publishes no end-of-life statement. migrate-v1 states verbatim: "V2 has three intentional breaking changes:" (new plugin API; new server API and client contracts; terminal config moves to one global cli.json), "V1 plugin implementations do not run in V2. Moving a file or renaming its config entry is not enough." and "Supported V1 functionality outside those areas is intended to remain compatible with V1." No stability page content exists at /v2/docs/. 2.0.32 publishes under plain latest, so v2 is shipped but not guaranteed, and the V1-compatibility sentence is an intent statement about V1, not a guarantee about V2.

Minimum supported versions: v1 floor 1.19.0 because 1.19.x is the first v1 line that knows about v2 config keys and rejects them explicitly, whereas 1.18.x silently strips them, making a misconfigured dual-compat install look healthy while doing the wrong thing; v2 floor 2.0.32 because it is the only 2.0.x measured anywhere in this run and every v2 contract finding was taken against it. The previously proposed 1.18.29 floor for object plugin entries is superseded by the 1.19.0 floor.

Pinning strategy: move @opencode-ai/plugin from 1.18.34 to exact 1.19.3 in both manifests (exact, not caret, because the minor moves in days); add @opencode/plugin@2.0.32 as a devDependency only in a separate optional group, never a runtime dependency, because plugins must stay runtime-import-free; resolve the undeclared zod that @opencode-ai/plugin re-exports either by declaring it at the host's major or by removing bare imports from plugin sources entirely so the question stops mattering; never attempt to unify the two dependencies since a single specifier cannot name two scopes.

Runtime version detection must come from the binary, never the environment, because on v2 the env a plugin sees comes from the background daemon rather than the invoking client. Parse major.minor.patch from opencode --version and reject any non-numeric core; accept major 1 with minor >= 19 and accept 2.0.32 or greater; reject everything else with a message naming that major's floor and the reason, and exit non-zero rather than warn-and-continue, since a silent misconfiguration on the wrong floor is indistinguishable from success.

Support-window policy: certify per v2 minor at .0 plus one pinned patch per calendar month, re-running the probe suite against 2.<minor>.0 when it appears and against the then-current latest patch at each month start and pinning exactly what passed; retest off-cycle immediately on any release whose notes touch the plugin definition shape, the session/message API, the config schema or run flags; drop v1 when opencode-ai@latest (the v1 line, not latest-1) has gone 30 or more days without a publish, a measurable trigger rather than a date; and record the tested set in one place so supported has an artifact behind it.
A compatibility claim is scoped to a tested version set; a host outside that set must be refused loudly, because on a fast-moving line a silent misconfiguration is indistinguishable from success.

direction: Using the latest-1 dist-tag as the v1 maintenance signal
reason: latest-1 for opencode-ai resolves to 1.1.4, an early-1.x line, not one major behind latest (1.19.3); the tag would have reported v1 abandoned roughly sixteen minors early.

direction: A single shared @opencode-ai/plugin dependency serving both host lines
reason: v2 ships under a different npm scope (@opencode/plugin, @opencode/cli); one specifier cannot name both packages, so the v2 leg needs its own declaration.

direction: Retesting on every new v2 release
reason: v2 currently publishes about 0.94 versions per day (33 versions in 35 days across a single minor), so a per-release cadence is arithmetically infeasible; per-minor-at-.0 plus one pinned patch per month replaces it.

direction: The 1.18.29 floor for object plugin entries
reason: Superseded by the 1.19.0 floor, which is a strict superset requirement; 1.18.29 adds nothing once 1.19.0 is required.

label: How often do the v1 and v2 lines release, and is v1 still maintained?
Separate npm scopes for v1 and v2
